note: UUID Extra makes the core uuid base field display-configurable via hook_entity_base_field_info_alter() (setDisplayConfigurable view+form) and hook_form_alter() (#access=TRUE when a uuid component exists), and ships a read-only 'uuid' field widget (UuidFieldWidget, disabled textfield) and a 'uuid' field formatter (UuidFieldFormatter, raw markup), both for field_type uuid. No settings form (configure=null), no permissions, no config, no Drush, no new plugin types. Persistent state is a 'uuid' component on core.entity_form_display.* (widget) or core.entity_view_display.* (formatter). Medium cases read back which display exposes uuid; hard cases add the component and verify the live display config.

evals.prompt: Drupal hides an entity's uuid base field from the display UIs. Using the uuid_extra module, how do I make a node's UUID appear as a field on its edit form and on its rendered display?
evals.expected_output: uuid_extra's hook_entity_base_field_info_alter() marks the uuid field setDisplayConfigurable for view and form, so it shows up on Manage form display and Manage display. Drag UUID out of Disabled, choose the 'UUID' widget (form) or 'UUID' formatter (display), and Save.

evals.prompt: What field widget and field formatter does uuid_extra provide, for which field type, and can an editor change the UUID using the widget?
evals.expected_output: It provides a field widget (plugin id 'uuid', UuidFieldWidget) and a field formatter (plugin id 'uuid', UuidFieldFormatter), both for the 'uuid' field type. The widget is a disabled/read-only textfield showing the current UUID, so an editor cannot change it; the formatter prints the raw UUID string as markup.

evals.prompt: Which hook does uuid_extra use to make the uuid base field configurable in the Manage form display / Manage display UIs, and what does it call on the field definition?
evals.expected_output: uuid_extra_entity_base_field_info_alter() looks up each entity type's uuid key field and calls setDisplayConfigurable('view', TRUE) and setDisplayConfigurable('form', TRUE) on it. A companion hook_form_alter() sets $form['uuid']['#access'] = TRUE when the form display has a uuid component.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, uuid_extra has been used to expose the node UUID as a field on exactly one content type's edit form. Inspect the live form-display configuration and name that content type.
evals.expected_output: Article. In core.entity_form_display.node.article.default there is a 'uuid' component using the 'uuid' widget, whereas other node types' form displays have no uuid component.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, is the node UUID currently configured to render on the Article content type's default view display? Inspect the live display configuration and answer yes or no.
evals.expected_output: Yes. core.entity_view_display.node.article.default has a 'uuid' component using the 'uuid' formatter, so the UUID renders on the Article default display.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use uuid_extra to expose the node UUID as a read-only field on the Article content type's default form display (the 'uuid' widget). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add a 'uuid' component with type 'uuid' to core.entity_form_display.node.article.default (via Manage form display in the UI, or setComponent('uuid', ['type' => 'uuid', ...])->save() in code). The UUID then shows as a disabled textfield on the Article edit form.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use uuid_extra to render the node UUID on the Article content type's default view display using its UUID formatter. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add a 'uuid' component with type 'uuid' to core.entity_view_display.node.article.default (via Manage display in the UI, or setComponent('uuid', ['type' => 'uuid', ...])->save() in code). The raw UUID string then renders on the Article default display.
